subject: May30 Weekly: priority highlights, QBR prep asks
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: leadership@redwood.ai; laura_bennett@redwood.ai; jonas_weber@redwood.ai; maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: May30 Weekly: priority highlights, QBR prep asks

Team —

Quick weekly snapshot heading into QBR week. Kept this tight so execs can scan quickly and act. TL;DR below, details and asks after.

TL;DR
- Wins: hosted API latency tail improved after kernel swap; ACME PoC demo scheduled.
- Risks: Dedicated capacity scaling tests uncovered a regression in autoscaler; several open SOC2 evidence items pending legal signoff.
- Asks: (1) Eng to prioritize autoscaler rollback plan (2) CS to confirm ACME success criteria and demo script (3) Finance to confirm QBR talking points re: ARR motions.

Wins (this week)
- Runtime: 12% reduction in P99 at 8k token seq after kernel selector update; baseline tests show stable mem usage. See perf summary in Drive link.
- Sales/CS: ACME Analytics PoC is booked for June 2nd demo; they validated embedding quality on 10k docs.
- Ops: Preflight for eu-west region went smooth; cold-start times under target for most models.

Risks / Hotspots
- Dedicated autoscaler: under certain traffic shapes the new scaling policy spikes GPU churn; risk to SLA if we roll without rollback path. (Assigned to Jonas)
- Compliance: SOC2 item #14 (data retention policy language) still awaiting final legal redline — blocker for several enterprise deals. (Assigned to Maya + Legal)
- QBR narrative gap: we need a short customer story (3 bullets) showing cost-savings for a large customer.

Asks / Action Items (owner | due)
- Jonas: push a canary rollback and run the synthetic capacity test (due: 2027-05-31 EOD).
- Maya: confirm ACME demo script and success criteria; capture a 2-slide customer impact snippet for QBR (due: 2027-06-01).
- Laura: one slide on engineering investments and timeline for autoscaler fixes (due: 2027-06-01 AM).
- Finance/Product: provide the ARR change narrative (1 paragraph) for QBR speaker notes (due: 2027-06-01).

Attachments: QBR_prep_deck_v2.pptx (draft), support_log_export_20270529.csv (ops).

Thanks — I want short confirmations on owners above so I can fold into the exec pack.

—
Karthik Iyer
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>; leadership@redwood.ai; jonas_weber@redwood.ai; maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: May30 Weekly: priority highlights, QBR prep asks

Thanks Karthik — concise and useful. A few quick notes from Eng: 

- Autoscaler: we can ship a short-term mitigation (disable predictive scaling for burst windows) that reduces churn and keeps latency stable. That would be a configuration flip and a short canary (agree with Jonas' rollback route).
- Timeline: we can have the mitigation ready by 2027-05-31 AM; full fix scoped for mid-June. I will add a one-slide summary for QBR (will include brief tradeoffs).

Agree we should prioritize the customer impact snippet. If Maya can provide ACME bullets, we can anonymize and include in the revenue slide.

Cc'ing Eng leads to pick up detailed runbook updates.

-Laura

Laura Bennett
VP, Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>; laura_bennett@redwood.ai; maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 09:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: May30 Weekly: priority highlights, QBR prep asks

Quick status on autoscaler work: started the canary rollback plan this morning. Steps executed:
- Rolled kernel selector to previous stable commit in canary pool (10% of capacity).
- Running synthetic traffic scenarios (burst, steady, tail-heavy) — early results look stable; P99 uplift reduced to within target.

Next steps: full capacity synthetic run tonight; will post logs to the shared Drive and link to the synthetics page. If green, I'll coordinate a controlled flip with Ops for 2027-06-01 02:00 UTC.

Also flagged: the root cause points to interaction between scaling heuristics and model warmup timing — we'll include a one-slide technical note for QBR to explain the mitigation.

Jonas

Jonas Weber
Head of Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>; laura_bennett@redwood.ai; jonas_weber@redwood.ai; leadership@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 11:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: May30 Weekly: priority highlights, QBR prep asks

All — update from CS and commercial side ahead of QBR pack finalization.

ACME Demo: confirmed for 2027-06-02 10:00 PT; success criteria agreed (embedding recall > 89% on their curated set; inference latency < 350ms for 512 tokens). I've attached the ACME demo script to the shared Drive and pulled two anonymized customer impact bullets:
- "Reduced search latency and storage costs by ~28% via prefix caching and batch compression."
- "Reduced per-query latency variance leading to 24% fewer timeouts during peak."

Compliance: Legal is queueing SOC2 evidence items — I have a short list (data retention language, subcontractor matrix, key rotation logs). I'll work with Laura to mark what Eng can ship vs. what needs Legal signoff.

Final asks from me: 
- Karthik: please include the two anonymized bullets on the customer impact slide; we should have them as a single-sentence pull quote (fine to anonymize).
- Finance/Product: can someone add the ARR delta line to slide 3 in the deck? (Whoever owns the pack: please confirm.)

I'll be on the demo with ACME and will bring back a short post-demo note we can drop into the QBR brief.

—
Maya Srinivasan
Head of Customer Success
Redwood Inference
